column1: # beats-2026: a beat-stratified sample of real headlines, labeled blind under docs/benchmark/codebook.md (codebook version 3).

# 384 rows drawn on 2026-10-11 from fixtures/headlines/harvested-live-intake.tsv (headlines harvested up to 2026-10-07; the intake's detector-guess column was not read), seven beats, quotas per outlet; within an outlet, rows sorted by sha256 of the lowercased headline and the first N taken.

# Labeller: a single model reviewer, labeling against the codebook text without seeing the detector's output. These labels are model-produced. A person spot-checks 50 random rows plus every row the reviewer marked unsure; a row a person has checked gets labeller 'owner'.

# Article type: from the outlet's own feed category or link section where the item was still in the feed on 2026-10-11 (typeSource publisher-tag), or from a web lookup for rows whose opinion_as_fact label depended on it (typeSource web-lookup:<url>). Everything else is unknown and judged on the headline alone (codebook rule 2).

# Not a fresh test set: the intake was committed with rule pack 1, the detector had been run over it, and 18 rule-pack phrases (such as "fans aren't happy") match intake headlines and nothing else in the labeled corpora. The rules may have been written with these headlines in view, so the benchmark treats this set like harvested.tsv: a regression check whose held-out numbers may be optimistic.
# Labels change only under a new codebook version. The note column gives the reviewer's reason in a few words; 'unsure' marks a row sent to a person to decide.
